title: Support zoom, reflow, and text resizing
summary: Interfaces should remain usable when users enlarge content or view the page at a narrow effective width.
guidance: Avoid fixed-height text containers and test content at 200% zoom and narrow viewport widths.
Let text wrap without clipping controls, labels, or essential instructions.

title: Reflow content without losing information
summary: Responsive layouts must preserve essential content and actions at narrow widths rather than relying on horizontal page scrolling.
guidance: At narrow viewports, reflow columns, wrap content, or provide a scoped overflow region for genuinely tabular data.
Check that headings, navigation, forms, and primary actions remain available at 320 CSS pixels and with text zoom.

title: Use weight and size before decorative text effects
summary: Clear typographic hierarchy remains legible across devices and does not depend on text shadows, outlines, or excessive letter spacing.
guidance: Differentiate hierarchy with a limited set of font sizes and weights, then use color as a supporting cue.
Reserve all-caps and expanded tracking for short labels; avoid applying them to long copy or small text.

title: Design default, hover, focus, active, and disabled states
summary: A component is incomplete if it communicates only its resting appearance.
guidance: Define state treatments for pointer, keyboard, pressed, loading, and unavailable conditions as appropriate.
Keep state changes perceivable without relying on color alone and preserve layout stability during loading.

title: Treat text truncation as an exception
summary: Truncated labels can conceal meaning and make navigation or data difficult to identify.
guidance: Prefer wrapping or a wider layout for meaningful content; truncate only predictable single-line labels.
When truncation is necessary, provide the full value through an accessible name and a usable disclosure mechanism.

title: Communicate progress for actions that take time
summary: Visible progress and a clear completion state prevent duplicate submissions and uncertainty.
guidance: Show a concise pending state, prevent accidental duplicate actions, and restore a usable state if the operation fails.
For indeterminate work, explain what is happening without inventing a percentage or blocking unrelated navigation.

title: Use product imagery to explain the experience
summary: Screenshots and illustrations should clarify a product workflow rather than act as generic decoration.
guidance: Show the interface or outcome relevant to the adjacent claim and use captions when context is not self-evident.
Ensure important explanatory text is available as text and do not bake critical copy into an image.

title: Document component states alongside appearance
summary: Design-system guidance is incomplete when it shows only a static default state.
guidance: Document keyboard focus, loading, empty, error, disabled, and responsive behavior for interactive patterns.
Add examples for long labels, localization, and high-density content where these can change the component contract.

title: Make mobile navigation operable and stateful
summary: A compact menu must communicate its state and preserve a reliable keyboard and touch interaction path.
guidance: Give the menu trigger an accessible name and expanded state, and make dismissal and focus return predictable.
Avoid hiding the only route to a critical action or relying on hover to reveal destinations.

title: Define a compact, semantic type scale
summary: A small type scale creates consistent hierarchy and makes responsive adjustments maintainable.
guidance: Define named text roles for display, headings, body, labels, and supporting text rather than styling each element independently.
Use fluid sizing only within intentional minimum and maximum bounds, and preserve readable body text on narrow screens.

title: Avoid low-contrast placeholder and helper text
summary: Muted supporting text can become unreadable when contrast is sacrificed to make a screen appear visually quiet.
guidance: Measure contrast for helper, placeholder, caption, and disabled text against their actual backgrounds.
Reduce visual prominence with size or spacing only when minimum readability remains intact.

title: Align related content to shared layout rails
summary: Shared alignment helps users connect navigation, page titles, content, and actions across a product.
guidance: Establish consistent horizontal content rails for headers, main sections, and footers.
When a data table needs a wider region, make the overflow or alternate layout intentional instead of silently shifting columns.

title: Optimize line length for sustained reading
summary: Long lines make it harder to track text, especially in paragraphs, documentation, and editorial content.
guidance: Constrain paragraph width to a comfortable measure and allow headings to use a separate, wider measure when appropriate.
Check line wrapping at narrow and wide viewport sizes instead of relying on a single desktop screenshot.

title: Reuse the project’s established design tokens
summary: Existing tokens preserve product identity and reduce divergence between new and established interface areas.
guidance: Inspect the project’s current color, typography, spacing, radius, and elevation tokens before adding styles.
Extend the existing token model with the smallest justified addition instead of introducing a competing palette.

title: Use whitespace to expose structure, not hide content
summary: Whitespace can clarify relationships but should not force frequent scrolling through low-density layouts.
guidance: Use larger gaps between sections than between tightly related controls, and keep repeated cards internally consistent.
For task-oriented dashboards, prioritize compact scanability while preserving adequate target and text spacing.
